## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Maccupāsamuttipañha* ("The Snare of Death") is a discourse in the *Milindapañha* belonging to the Late Sutta collection [SuttaCentral]. Set as a dialogue between King Milinda and the arahant elder Nāgasena in the royal city of Sāgala, the section is drawn upon in secondary discussions concerning the doctrinal function and efficacy of *paritta* (protective verses) [Si Ti La 2014].

According to SuttaCentral, related textual material and thematic citations correspond to verse 128 of the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 128), the *Garuḍapurāṇa* (1.113.20), various versions of the *Udānavarga* (including UV 1, the Tibetan *Uv Kg* 1, and Chinese translations T 210.1, T 212.1, and T 213.1), the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and the *Rudrāyaṇāvadāna* of the *Divyāvadāna* [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus shows substantial internal reuse across 18 other Pali texts, sharing extensive stock phrasing with other sections of the *Milindapañha* such as the *Maccubhāyanābhāyanapañha* (Mil 5.2.3), *Dhammābhisamayapañha* (Mil 6.3.8), *Katādhikārasaphalapañha* (Mil 5.1.1), and *Gabbhāvakkantipañha* (Mil 5.1.6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also notes minor cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Sarvadurgatipariśodhanatejorājā* (D0483) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
